subject: netguard is not persistent: a reboot or libvirtd restart silently removes team isolation
description:
Found while applying netguard 2026-09-26. netguard.sh installs an iptables chain and an ebtables among-rule, and libvirt REWRITES its own chains on restart, so isolation disappears with no error and no sign - the boxes simply become mutually reachable again mid-event. Re-running the script is safe and idempotent (both chains are flushed and rebuilt), so the fix is a systemd unit ordered After=libvirtd.service that runs it, plus ideally a periodic re-assert. NOT done deliberately: adding a unit to a production host's boot path is an operator decision, not something to assume while they are not looking. Until then, re-run 'sudo bash /srv/hexworth/engine1/provision/netguard.sh' after any reboot or libvirtd restart and re-verify FROM INSIDE A BOX, because the script's own success output cannot distinguish an enforced rule from an inert one - that is exactly how the first version shipped a no-op.
[2026-09-26 20:03] RESOLVED 2026-09-26. engine1-netguard.service (Type=oneshot, PartOf=libvirtd.service, WantedBy=multi-user.target) plus engine1-netguard.timer (OnCalendar=*:0/5, Persistent=true) installed and enabled on bc2; units committed to _tools/engine1/systemd/. netguard.sh gained --ensure, which checks structurally and rebuilds ONLY on drift, so re-asserting every 5 min costs nothing and never opens the flush window a plain run has. TWO OF MY OWN UNITS REPORTED HEALTHY WHILE DOING NOTHING, which is worth recording because it is the same shape as the bug netguard shipped with: (1) OnUnitActiveSec never scheduled because RemainAfterExit kept the service permanently active, so NextElapseUSecMonotonic=infinity and the timer would never fire again while is-enabled and is-active both said fine; (2) after switching to OnCalendar the timer fired but the service still did not run, because systemd will not re-trigger an already-active oneshot nor schedule the next elapse while its unit is active - list-timers showed LAST fired, the journal showed no run. RemainAfterExit is incompatible with a repeating timer; removed. PROVEN: --ensure no-ops when correct and repairs after a manual flush; libvirtd restart kept 7/7 domains running and PartOf re-ran the unit with the guard intact; the timer fired unattended at 15:55:01 and actually ran the service; SELF-HEAL end to end, both chains flushed at 15:56:08 and repaired by the timer at 16:00:06 with no intervention; functional isolation from inside a box False/False/False afterwards; all six terminals 200 on their real token paths throughout. CORRECTION to this item's own premise: libvirtd restart does NOT wipe ENGINE1GUARD - libvirt rewrites its OWN chains, and the custom chain plus its FORWARD jump survive. The case that definitely loses everything is a REBOOT, since neither iptables nor ebtables persists by default, and that is what the enabled unit covers. REBOOT IS NOT TESTED because bc2 runs the live tournament; that is the one remaining unverified claim here. Max exposure after an unexpected flush is the 5-minute timer interval, not indefinite.
